title: Thenar Recovery After Carpal Tunnel Release with a Silent Cervical Radiculopathy: Three Explanations for Double Crush
content: Electrodiagnostic testing often finds a cervical radiculopathy together with a median neuropathy at the wrist, but coexistence does not show that the lesions interact. A clinically silent C8 or T1 radiculopathy, identified by needle electromyography, may predict incomplete thenar motor recovery after carpal tunnel release without reducing the improvement in symptoms. We distinguish independent lesion burdens, a nonlinear relation between remaining motor capacity and measured function, and biological interaction in which one lesion alters susceptibility or recovery at the other; these explanations can coexist. A numerical illustration shows that independent losses can produce an apparent interaction in measured strength when compensation is exhausted, so a statistical interaction does not establish biological interaction. Compound muscle action potential amplitude does not count surviving axons, and the neurophysiological grade of the wrist lesion is ordinal. We propose a prospective study using standardized nerve conduction studies and needle electromyography at both sites, with serial quantitative thenar strength. The first test is prognostic: whether a matched root lesion adds information about six-month strength beyond baseline function and focal wrist findings. Motor unit estimates paired with force could examine compensation directly.
